title: Newcastle’s Sven Botman undergoes surgery on facial fracture, hoping to return before end of season
content:
Newcastle United centre-back Sven Botman has undergone surgery after suffering a head injury during the club’s derby defeat to Sunderland on Sunday.

Botman, 26, was substituted as part of a concussion protocol in the 54th minute of Newcastle’s 2-1 loss and was replaced by Malick Thiaw.

The former Netherlands Under-21 international, who signed a new long-term contract at Newcastle in January, is now in recovery, but the club’s medical department do not anticipate a long-term absence.

“Sven Botman has undergone successful surgery on a facial fracture,” Newcastle said in a statement on Monday.

“Sven is not expected to be sidelined for an extended period and hopes to be available again during the closing weeks of the season.”

Any time on the sidelines would represent a blow to Eddie Howe, whose squad has been riven by injury this season, particularly in defence, although the head coach hopes to have Bruno Guimaraes, Lewis Miley, Sandro Tonali and Fabian Schar in contention for their next Premier League fixture, away to Crystal Palace on April 12.

It doesn’t rain but it pours for Howe and Newcastle. Fresh from their disastrous result against Sunderland comes the news that another senior player faces a spell out of action.

Botman’s substitution as St James’ Park was followed three minutes later by Sunderland’s equaliser. The two things do not necessarily go together, but Thiaw’s performance when he came onto the pitch reeked of fatigue.

Botman is a quality player whose spell on Tyneside has been undermined by repeated injuries and fitness issues. He cannot catch a break.

While it is good news that he has been operated on swiftly, Howe needs as many options as possible as he seeks some sort of uplift for the remainder of the season.
